craft_evidence.owned: yes, evidence: the brand names its Gloucester shirt factory ("devotedly handmade in our factory just outside of Gloucester", understanding-our-shirts; "our Gloucester workrooms", royal-warrant and sustainability pages), names staff there (Bette Elton and Kathleen Cope, Gloucester factory since 1964, our-people page) with workshop photographs; press locates it at Quedgeley, Gloucestershire, ~100 staff (The Manufacturer, 22 Feb 2013; Punchline Gloucester 21 Oct 2019 on filings). Ties are made in a second owned workroom in Kent (Sidcup). No street address on the brand site.
craft_evidence.makers: no: PDPs name no factory or maker; "Country Of Origin" only
craft_evidence.mills: no: no mill named on any PDP read; "Sea Island Quality Cotton" and "Escorial" wool are fibre/cloth grades; sustainability page says mills hold OEKO-TEX, European Flax, RWS and GOTS certifications without naming them
craft_evidence.madein: 87 of 107 PDPs sampled (81%) state Country Of Origin: Italy 63 (tailoring, trousers, outerwear, knits), United Kingdom 19 (mostly nightwear and some shirts), Netherlands 4 (suits), US 1; ready-to-wear shirts mostly state none (11 of 16 shirt PDPs sampled); brand pages say shirts and ties are made in Gloucester
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: founded 1885 by John Arthur Turnbull and Ernest Asser (our-people page); at 71-72 Jermyn Street since 1903 (jermyn page); Royal Warrant from the then Prince of Wales in 1980 (royal-warrant page)
craft_evidence.process: yes: 33 hand-cut pieces per shirt, non-fused collars with woven bias-cut interlining, Australian mother-of-pearl buttons with crossed-lock stitching (understanding-our-shirts); Made in England blog: pattern-cutting, cutting and sewing by specialists, ~40 min sewing per ready-to-wear shirt
craft_evidence.reasoning: The brand owns and names its Gloucester shirt factory (Quedgeley), shows its workroom and named long-serving staff, and documents shirt construction specifically (33 hand-cut pieces, non-fused collars), with dated heritage since 1885 and Jermyn Street since 1903. That is maker-and-brand-the-same for shirts and ties, but tailoring, trousers, outerwear and knitwear (about 22% of styles) are stated as made in Italy or the Netherlands by unnamed makers, and no mill is named, so 4 rather than 5.

ownership.owner: Fayed family: Companies House PSC register for Turnbull & Asser Limited (01066321) lists James Allie Fayed (25-50% shares, 50-75% votes, right to appoint directors; notified 25 Apr 2026) and Liam Fayed (25-50%; notified 26 Jun 2026); the brand calls itself "Family-run"
